subject: Status: benchmark repro done; where GIFT wins and where it doesn't
body:
Hi both,

Repro is done on the natural-distribution-shift benchmark. Headline numbers: with intermediate data available, iterative self-training alone recovers most of the drop, confirming the implicit-curriculum effect from the paper. Without intermediates - the realistic customer case - plain self-training falls short, and GIFT's interpolated virtual samples buy us +2.3 points of target accuracy over it on our repro, in line with the published finding. Stacking GIFT on top of a standard domain-adaptation baseline also improved target accuracy, which is the config I want for the pilot.

Risk for the pilot: when source and target are too far apart, the interpolation curriculum needs more steps and cost grows roughly linearly - our worst sweep took 5x the compute of the best. Amara and I will publish a cost-vs-shift table next week so we can set customer expectations honestly.

Katya
